questions.question: How many tonnes of gold have been mined in all of human history, as of the end of 2025?
questions.explainer: Roughly 220,000 tonnes of gold have ever been mined, which would form a cube only about 22 metres on each side, and about two-thirds of it was dug up after 1950.
questions.source_title: How much gold has been mined? - World Gold Council

questions.question: How many years ago did Ötzi the Iceman, found frozen in the Alps in 1991, die?
questions.explainer: Ötzi lived between about 3350 and 3105 BC, roughly 5,300 years ago, centuries before the Great Pyramid or Stonehenge's sarsen circle. He still had an arrowhead in his shoulder.

questions.question: How many international migrants (people living outside the country they were born in) were there worldwide in 2024?
questions.explainer: Migrants are about 3.7% of humanity; if they formed one country it would be the fourth most populous on Earth.

questions.question: What is the total area of Greenland, the world's largest island?
questions.explainer: Greenland is about three times the size of Texas, but roughly 80% of it is buried under an ice sheet up to 3 km thick.

questions.question: What was the average price of a Big Mac in the United States in July 2024, according to The Economist's Big Mac index?
questions.explainer: The Economist has tracked burger prices since 1986 as a light-hearted guide to currency values. The US Big Mac passed $6 in 2025.
questions.source_title: The Economist - Big Mac index data (big-mac-raw-index.csv, USA, 2024-07-01)

questions.question: How many Concorde supersonic airliners were built in total, including prototypes?
questions.explainer: Just 20 Concordes were built: two prototypes, two pre-production aircraft and 16 production models, 14 of which flew passengers for British Airways and Air France.

questions.question: How many minutes did Yuri Gagarin's 1961 spaceflight last, from launch to landing?
questions.explainer: The first human spaceflight was a single orbit of Earth lasting about 108 minutes, shorter than most feature films.

questions.question: How many metres below sea level is the surface of the Dead Sea, as of 2025?
questions.explainer: The Dead Sea's shores are the lowest land on Earth, and the lake is still dropping by more than a metre a year as the Jordan River's inflow is diverted upstream.

questions.question: How many people worldwide were living with HIV at the end of 2023?
questions.explainer: About 1.3 million people were newly infected and 630,000 died of AIDS-related illnesses that year, while roughly 77% of people with HIV were on treatment.
questions.source_title: Global HIV & AIDS statistics — Fact sheet (UNAIDS)

questions.question: How many copies of the Harry Potter books had been sold worldwide as of 2023?
questions.explainer: More than 600 million Harry Potter books have been sold in over 80 languages, the best-selling book series ever: enough for one copy for every 13 people alive.

questions.question: How much prize money did FIFA pay Argentina for winning the 2022 World Cup, in US$?
questions.explainer: Taken from a total prize pot of US$440 million. Even teams knocked out in the group stage collected US$9 million each.
questions.source_title: 2022 World Cup Prize Money (Associated Press via WTOP)

questions.question: How many Scoville heat units does Pepper X, certified the world's hottest chili pepper by Guinness in 2023, average?
questions.explainer: That is several hundred times hotter than a jalapeño (2,500-8,000 SHU) and in the same league as police pepper spray.
questions.source_title: Guinness World Records - Hottest chili pepper

questions.question: How many characters are encoded in version 16.0 of the Unicode Standard, released in September 2024?
questions.explainer: Unicode 16.0 added 5,185 characters, including 3,995 Egyptian hieroglyphs; emoji make up fewer than 4,000 of the total, while CJK ideographs account for nearly 100,000.
questions.source_title: Announcing The Unicode Standard, Version 16.0 (Unicode Blog)

questions.question: How many trees are there on Earth, according to the 2015 global estimate published in Nature?
questions.explainer: About 3.04 trillion, roughly 400 trees per person, though the total has fallen by around 46% since the dawn of agriculture.
questions.source_title: Mapping tree density at a global scale - Nature (Crowther et al. 2015)

questions.question: How many different items does the average US supermarket carry, as of 2023?
questions.explainer: The average store stocks almost 32,000 distinct products, yet a typical weekly shop touches only a few dozen of them.
questions.source_title: FMI - The Food Industry Association: Supermarket Facts

questions.question: How much money is a one-tonne pile of US pennies worth?
questions.explainer: A penny weighs 2.5 g, so a tonne (1,000,000 g) is 400,000 pennies, worth $4,000.

questions.question: Spending $1,000 a day, how many years would it take to get through a billion dollars?
questions.explainer: A billion divided by $1,000 a day is a million days, which is about 2,700 years. You would have started around the founding of Rome.

questions.question: How many drops of water are in an Olympic swimming pool?
questions.explainer: An Olympic pool holds 2.5 million litres, which is 2.5 billion millilitres. A drop is about 0.05 ml, so about 50 billion drops.

questions.question: How many litres of blood does your heart pump in a day?
questions.explainer: The heart pumps about 5 litres a minute at rest, which is 300 litres an hour and about 7,200 litres a day.

questions.question: How many days would it take to watch all 236 episodes of Friends back to back?
questions.explainer: 236 episodes of about 22 minutes is 5,192 minutes, 87 hours: about three and a half days.

questions.question: How many Oscar statuettes would weigh the same as an African elephant?
questions.explainer: An Oscar weighs 3.86 kg and a big elephant about 6,000 kg, so about 1,600 statuettes.
questions.source_title: The Oscar statuette (Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences)

questions.question: How many times could the world's undersea internet cables wrap around the Earth?
questions.explainer: There are about 1.4 million km of submarine cable in service. The equator is 40,075 km, so about 35 times around.

questions.question: How many times would all the walls of the Great Wall of China stretch from New York to Los Angeles?
questions.explainer: China's 2012 survey measured 21,196 km of wall. New York to Los Angeles is about 3,944 km as the crow flies, so the Wall would make the trip about 5.4 times.

questions.question: If you use your phone five hours a day from age 15 to 80, how many whole years of your life is that?
questions.explainer: Five hours is 5/24 of a day. Over 65 years that adds up to about 14 years spent looking at a screen.
questions.source_title: Study finds the average American spent 2.5 months on their phone in 2024 (Reviews.org)

questions.question: If a medieval monk copied one page a day, how many years would it take to copy the whole Bible by hand?
questions.explainer: A full Bible runs to about 1,200 printed pages. One page a day, every day, is about 3.3 years for a single copy.

questions.question: Walking 25 km a day, how many years would it take to walk every section of the Great Wall of China?
questions.explainer: China's survey measured 21,196 km of wall. At 25 km a day that is 848 days, about 2.3 years.

questions.question: How many days would it take to binge every episode of The Simpsons back to back?
questions.explainer: By May 2025 there were 790 episodes of about 22 minutes: 290 hours, which is about 12 days without sleep.

questions.question: How many Moons lined up side by side would it take to reach from the Earth to the Sun?
questions.explainer: The Sun is 149.6 million km away and the Moon is 3,474 km across, so about 43,000 Moons would bridge the gap.

questions.question: If the Sun were shrunk to a 24 cm basketball, how many metres away would the Earth be?
questions.explainer: The Sun is 1,392,700 km across and the Earth is 149.6 million km away, 107 Sun-widths. 107 × 0.24 m is about 26 metres.

questions.question: How many Greater Londons would fit inside Australia?
questions.explainer: Australia covers about 7,692,000 km² and Greater London about 1,572 km², so Australia could swallow roughly 4,900 Londons.

questions.question: At four minutes a day, how many full days of an 80-year life are spent brushing teeth?
questions.explainer: Four minutes a day for 80 years is 116,880 minutes. Divided by 1,440 minutes in a day that is about 81 days of brushing.

questions.question: How many Amazon packages are delivered in the United States every minute?
questions.explainer: Amazon delivered about 5.9 billion packages in the US in 2023. A year has 525,960 minutes, so about 11,000 packages a minute.
questions.source_title: Amazon tops UPS and FedEx in US deliveries (Fortune)

questions.question: How many breaths do you take in a year?
questions.explainer: At rest an adult breathes about 16 times a minute: 23,000 breaths a day and about 8.4 million a year.

questions.question: How many sheets of printer paper stacked up would reach the top of the Eiffel Tower?
questions.explainer: Ordinary 80 gsm paper is about 0.1 mm thick and the Eiffel Tower is 330 m tall, so you would need about 3.3 million sheets.

questions.question: How many times more people are alive today than in the year AD 1?
questions.explainer: Estimates put the world's population in AD 1 at about 300 million. Today's 8.1 billion is about 27 times more.

questions.question: How many Titanics would it take to equal the weight of the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.explainer: The Great Pyramid weighs about 5.9 million tonnes and the Titanic displaced about 52,000 tonnes, so about 110 Titanics.

questions.question: How many people could a blue whale's 150 tonnes feed, at 500 g of meat each?
questions.explainer: 150 tonnes is 150,000 kg. At half a kilo per plate that is 300,000 servings, a whole city's dinner.

questions.question: How many Earths could you fit inside the Sun, by volume?
questions.explainer: The Sun's volume is about 1.41 × 10¹⁸ km³ and Earth's is 1.08 × 10¹² km³, so about 1.3 million Earths would fit inside.

questions.question: Saving $10 every day from your 18th birthday, how much cash would you have on your 65th, with no interest?
questions.explainer: 47 years is 17,167 days. At $10 a day that is about $172,000 under the mattress.

questions.question: How many standard 12.4 kg gold bars are stored in Fort Knox?
questions.explainer: Fort Knox holds about 4,580 tonnes of gold, which is 4.58 million kg. Divided by 12.4 kg a bar, that is about 370,000 bars.

questions.question: How many Olympic gold medals' worth of real gold is in one standard 12.4 kg gold bar?
questions.explainer: A Paris 2024 gold medal contains just 6 g of gold on a silver core. A 12.4 kg bar holds about 2,100 medals' worth.

questions.question: How many 75-year lifetimes fit between the building of the Great Pyramid and today?
questions.explainer: The Great Pyramid was finished around 2560 BC, about 4,570 years ago. Divided by a 75-year life, that is only about 61 lifetimes end to end.

questions.question: If everyone on Earth held hands in one long line, how many times would it wrap around the equator?
questions.explainer: 8.1 billion people with arms spread about 1.5 m is 12 billion metres, 12 million km. The equator is 40,075 km, so about 300 times around.

questions.question: Flying at a jumbo jet's 900 km/h, how many years would it take to reach the Sun?
questions.explainer: The Sun is about 149.6 million km away. At 900 km/h that is 166,000 hours, which is about 19 years in the air.

questions.question: If all the hot dogs sold at Major League Baseball games in one season were laid end to end, how many km would they stretch?
questions.explainer: Fans ate about 19.1 million ballpark hot dogs in 2022. At 15 cm each that is 2.9 million metres, about 2,900 km: New York to Denver.

questions.question: Driving eight hours a day at 60 km/h, how many years would it take to drive every road in the United States?
questions.explainer: The US has about 6.7 million km of public roads. At 480 km a day that is 14,000 days, about 38 years.

questions.question: Reading one English Wikipedia article a minute without stopping, how many years would it take to read them all?
questions.explainer: English Wikipedia passed 7 million articles in 2025. At one a minute that is 7 million minutes, about 13 years with no sleep.

questions.question: How many iPhones, stacked flat on top of each other, would it take to reach the International Space Station?
questions.explainer: The ISS orbits about 400 km up and an iPhone 15 is 7.8 mm thick. 400,000 m divided by 0.0078 m is about 51 million phones.

questions.question: How many sugar cubes are dissolved in a 2-litre bottle of Coca-Cola?
questions.explainer: Classic Coke has 10.6 g of sugar per 100 ml, so 212 g in 2 litres. At 4 g a cube that is about 53 sugar cubes.

questions.question: How many grains of rice are in a 1 kg bag?
questions.explainer: A grain of long-grain rice weighs about 25 mg, so 1,000 g divided by 0.025 g is roughly 40,000 grains.

questions.question: How many Earths would fit side by side across the face of the Sun?
questions.explainer: The Sun is about 1,392,700 km across and Earth is 12,742 km, so about 109 Earths would line up across it.

questions.question: How many Rubik's Cubes stacked on top of each other would reach the top of the Burj Khalifa?
questions.explainer: A Rubik's Cube is 5.7 cm on a side and the Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall, so about 15,000 cubes.

questions.question: How many days would Japan's fastest bullet train, at its 320 km/h service speed, take to reach the Moon?
questions.explainer: The Moon is 384,400 km away. At 320 km/h that is 1,201 hours, or about 50 days.

questions.question: How many Big Macs' worth of energy does a runner burn in a marathon?
questions.explainer: A marathon burns about 2,600 kcal and a Big Mac has 590 kcal, so a marathon is about four and a half Big Macs.

questions.question: How many LEGO bricks stacked on top of each other would reach the top of the Eiffel Tower?
questions.explainer: A LEGO brick is 9.6 mm tall and the Eiffel Tower is 330 m, so about 34,000 bricks.

questions.question: How many times will your heart beat in an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: At 70 beats a minute that is 100,800 a day, 36.8 million a year, and about 2.9 billion over 80 years.

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools would the stone of the Great Pyramid fill?
questions.explainer: The pyramid's volume is about 2.6 million m³. An Olympic pool holds 2,500 m³, so about 1,000 pools of solid stone.

questions.question: How many years of an 80-year life does the average American spend on their phone, at five hours a day?
questions.explainer: Five hours a day is 5/24 of each day. Over 80 years that is about 17 years of scrolling.
questions.source_title: Study finds the average American spent 2.5 months on their phone in 2024 (Reviews.org)

questions.question: How many 250 ml glasses of milk does one dairy cow give in a day?
questions.explainer: A modern dairy cow gives about 28 litres a day. Divided into 250 ml glasses, that is about 110 glasses.

questions.question: How many shipping containers does the Port of Shanghai, the world's busiest, handle every minute?
questions.explainer: Shanghai handled 51.5 million standard containers in 2024. A year has 525,960 minutes, so about 98 containers a minute.

questions.question: The Pacific plate carries Hawaii towards Japan at about 7 cm a year. How many years until they meet?
questions.explainer: Honolulu to Tokyo is about 6,200 km, or 6.2 million metres. At 0.07 m a year that is roughly 89 million years.

questions.question: How many mosquito bites would it take to drain all the blood from an adult?
questions.explainer: A mosquito drinks about 5 microlitres (0.000005 litres) and an adult has about 5 litres of blood, so about a million bites.

questions.question: How many Earths could you pack inside Jupiter, by volume?
questions.explainer: Jupiter's volume is about 1.43 × 10¹⁵ km³ and Earth's is 1.08 × 10¹² km³, so about 1,300 Earths would fit inside.

questions.question: How many sugar cubes would weigh the same as an African elephant?
questions.explainer: A big African elephant weighs about 6 tonnes (6,000 kg) and a sugar cube about 4 g, so about 1.5 million cubes.

questions.question: How many seconds are there in a year?
questions.explainer: There are 86,400 seconds in a day and 365.25 days in a year, which gives about 31.6 million seconds.

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools of water go over Niagara Falls every minute?
questions.explainer: About 2,400 m³ goes over the falls every second, so 144,000 m³ a minute. An Olympic pool is 2,500 m³, so about 58 pools a minute.

questions.question: How many bananas could Elon Musk buy with his entire 2025 fortune, at 25 cents each?
questions.explainer: Forbes put Musk's fortune at about $342 billion in 2025. At $0.25 a banana that is about 1.4 trillion bananas, 170 for every person alive.

questions.question: At a garden snail's top speed, how many years would it take one to cross the United States?
questions.explainer: Researchers clocked garden snails at about 1 metre an hour flat out. Coast to coast is about 4,500 km, or 4.5 million hours: roughly 510 years.
questions.source_title: Snail's pace revealed in new study (ITV)

questions.question: How many people around the world share your birthday?
questions.explainer: 8.1 billion people divided across 365 days is about 22 million people blowing out candles on the same day as you.

questions.question: How many trees are there on Earth for every person?
questions.explainer: A 2015 census counted about 3.04 trillion trees. With 8.1 billion people, that is about 380 trees each.
questions.source_title: Mapping tree density at a global scale (Nature, 2015)

questions.question: How many years of an 80-year life are spent asleep?
questions.explainer: Eight hours a night is a third of each day, and a third of 80 years is about 27 years asleep.

questions.question: Reading aloud at 150 words a minute, how many hours would it take to read all seven Harry Potter books?
questions.explainer: The seven books total 1,084,170 words. At 150 words a minute that is 7,228 minutes, about 120 hours of reading aloud.
questions.source_title: How many words are in the Harry Potter books (Word Counter)

questions.question: If people stood shoulder to shoulder, half a metre each, in one line around the equator, how many people would it take?
questions.explainer: The equator is 40,075 km, or 40 million metres. At half a metre per person that is about 80 million people, roughly the population of Germany.

questions.question: If the Sun were shrunk to a 24 cm basketball, how many millimetres across would the Earth be?
questions.explainer: Earth is 12,742 km across and the Sun 1,392,700 km, a ratio of 109. A 240 mm ball divided by 109 is about 2.2 mm: a peppercorn.

questions.question: How many African elephants would it take to balance a blue whale on a giant seesaw?
questions.explainer: A blue whale can weigh 150 tonnes and a big elephant about 6 tonnes, so about 25 elephants.

questions.question: How many golf balls would fit inside a school bus?
questions.explainer: A bus interior is roughly 10 m × 2.5 m × 2.5 m, about 62 m³. A golf ball is 42.7 mm across (0.0000407 m³), and spheres pack to about 64% of the space, so about 980,000 balls.

questions.question: How many days would it take to watch the first 33 Marvel Cinematic Universe films back to back?
questions.explainer: The first 33 MCU films run 4,359 minutes in total, about 72.7 hours: three full days and nights of superheroes.
questions.source_title: How long would it take to watch all 33 MCU movies (Fiction Horizon)

questions.question: How many days of non-stop football is a full Premier League season?
questions.explainer: There are 380 matches a season, each about 90 minutes plus stoppages, call it 1.5 hours: 570 hours, which is about 24 days straight.

questions.question: Counting out loud at one person a second, how many years would it take to count everyone who has ever lived?
questions.explainer: About 117 billion people have ever been born. At one a second, with 31.6 million seconds in a year, that is about 3,700 years.
questions.source_title: How many people have ever lived on Earth? (PRB)

questions.question: How many emails are sent every second worldwide?
questions.explainer: About 361.6 billion emails were sent and received a day in 2024, which is about 4.2 million a second.

questions.question: How many kilograms does a million dollars in $100 bills weigh?
questions.explainer: A million dollars is 10,000 hundred-dollar bills, and each bill weighs about 1 gram: 10 kg, which fits in a backpack.

questions.question: How many tonnes of food does a person eat in a lifetime?
questions.explainer: Around 1.5 kg of food a day, times 365 days, times 80 years, is about 44,000 kg: 44 tonnes, or the weight of a Boeing 737.

questions.question: How many apples would it take to equal the weight of the International Space Station?
questions.explainer: The ISS has a mass of about 420 tonnes (420,000 kg). A medium apple is about 180 g, so that is roughly 2.3 million apples.

questions.question: At three and a half minutes a song, how many years would it take to listen to every track on Spotify?
questions.explainer: Spotify has more than 100 million tracks. 100 million × 3.5 minutes is 5.8 million hours, about 670 years.

questions.question: How many years is a trillion seconds?
questions.explainer: A year has about 31.6 million seconds, so a trillion seconds is about 32,000 years, back to the Ice Age.

questions.question: If every car in the world were parked bumper to bumper, how many times would the line wrap around the equator?
questions.explainer: There are about 1.5 billion cars, each about 4.5 m long: 6.75 billion metres, 6.75 million km. The equator is 40,075 km, so about 170 times round.

questions.question: How many Big Macs could the US federal government buy with one year's spending?
questions.explainer: Washington spent about $6.13 trillion in fiscal 2023. At $5.69 a Big Mac that is about 1.1 trillion burgers, 130 for everyone on Earth.

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools would all the tea Britain drinks in one day fill?
questions.explainer: Brits drink about 100 million cups a day. At 250 ml each that is 25 million litres, which is 10 Olympic pools.
questions.source_title: Tea loved by Brits (UK Tea & Infusions Association)

questions.question: How many 30 cm pizzas, laid flat side by side, would it take to cover the entire surface of the Moon?
questions.explainer: The Moon's surface is about 37.9 million km², or 3.79 × 10¹³ m². A 30 cm pizza covers 0.0707 m², so you would need about 540 trillion pizzas.

questions.question: If the Louvre's visitors for one year queued in single file, one metre apart, how many kilometres long would the queue be?
questions.explainer: The Louvre had about 8.7 million visitors in 2024. One per metre makes a queue 8.7 million metres long: 8,700 km, Paris to Beijing.

questions.question: How many sheets of A4 paper would weigh the same as an African elephant?
questions.explainer: A sheet of 80 gsm A4 paper weighs 5 g. An elephant of 6 tonnes is 6 million grams, so 1.2 million sheets.

questions.question: How many times faster is a modern airliner than the Wright brothers' first flight in 1903?
questions.explainer: The Wright Flyer's first hop averaged about 10.9 km/h. A jet cruises at about 900 km/h, roughly 83 times faster.

questions.question: How many centimetres do your fingernails grow over an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: Fingernails grow about 3.5 mm a month, which is 4.2 cm a year and about 340 cm over 80 years: a nail taller than a doorway.

questions.question: How many cups of tea could have been brewed from all the tea dumped at the Boston Tea Party?
questions.explainer: About 92,000 pounds of tea, roughly 42,000 kg, went into Boston Harbor in 1773. At 2 g a cup that is about 21 million cups.
questions.source_title: Boston Tea Party facts and numbers (Boston Tea Party Historical Society)

questions.question: If everyone on Earth stood together, four to a square metre, how many square kilometres would the crowd cover?
questions.explainer: 8.1 billion people at four per square metre need 2.0 billion m², which is about 2,000 km²: all of humanity fits inside Greater London.

questions.question: Driving non-stop at 100 km/h, how many years would it take to reach Mars at its closest approach?
questions.explainer: At their closest, Earth and Mars are about 54.6 million km apart. At 100 km/h that is 546,000 hours, which is about 62 years.

questions.question: How many Post-it notes would it take to cover a football pitch?
questions.explainer: A classic Post-it is 76 mm square, 0.0058 m². A pitch is about 7,140 m², so about 1.2 million notes.

questions.question: How many months of a standard Netflix subscription could one 30-second Super Bowl ad pay for?
questions.explainer: A 30-second Super Bowl spot cost about $7 million in 2024, and Netflix Standard was $15.49 a month: about 450,000 months, or 38,000 years of telly.

questions.question: How many cups of coffee does the average American drink between the ages of 20 and 80?
questions.explainer: Americans average about two cups a day. Over 60 years that is about 44,000 cups.

questions.question: How many pizzas do Americans eat every second?
questions.explainer: Americans get through about 3 billion pizzas a year. Divided by 31.6 million seconds, that is about 95 pizzas every second.

questions.question: How many Mount Everests stacked on top of each other would it take to reach the Moon?
questions.explainer: The Moon is on average 384,400 km away and Everest is 8.849 km tall, so you would need about 43,000 Everests in a pile.

questions.question: If Usain Bolt could hold his 100 m world-record pace for a whole marathon, how many minutes would it take him?
questions.explainer: Bolt ran 100 m in 9.58 s. A marathon is 421.95 of those, so 421.95 × 9.58 s is 4,042 s, about 67 minutes.

questions.question: How many hours does a person spend eating over an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: About an hour and a half a day at the table, times 365 days, times 80 years, is about 44,000 hours: five solid years of eating.

questions.question: Walking non-stop at 5 km/h, how many days would it take to walk the full length of the Nile?
questions.explainer: The Nile runs about 6,650 km. At 5 km/h that is 1,330 hours, which is about 55 days without a single break.

questions.question: How many hours of video are uploaded to YouTube every single hour?
questions.explainer: More than 500 hours of video are uploaded every minute, so about 30,000 hours of new video arrive every hour.
questions.source_title: Hours of video uploaded to YouTube every minute (Statista)

questions.question: How many LEGO bricks stacked one on top of another would reach the International Space Station?
questions.explainer: A LEGO brick is 9.6 mm tall and the ISS orbits about 400 km up. 400,000 m divided by 0.0096 m is about 42 million bricks.

questions.question: How many $5 lattes could Taylor Swift's Eras Tour ticket sales have bought?
questions.explainer: The Eras Tour grossed about $2.08 billion in ticket sales. At $5 a latte that is about 420 million coffees.

questions.question: How many 1.44 MB floppy disks would it take to hold what a 128 GB phone stores?
questions.explainer: 128 GB is 128,000 MB. Divided by 1.44 MB a disk that is about 89,000 floppies, a stack about 300 m tall.

questions.question: How many honeybees' entire lifetime output does it take to fill one 450 g jar of honey?
questions.explainer: One worker bee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its life, roughly 0.4 g. A 450 g jar is the life's work of about 1,100 bees.

questions.question: How many photos are taken worldwide every second?
questions.explainer: About 1.94 trillion photos were taken in 2024, almost all on phones. Divided by 31.6 million seconds that is about 61,000 photos a second.

questions.question: How many $799 iPhones could Apple have bought with its own 2024 revenue?
questions.explainer: Apple's revenue for fiscal 2024 was $391 billion. At $799 an iPhone 16 that is about 490 million phones.
questions.source_title: Apple reports fourth quarter results (Apple Newsroom)

questions.question: Walking 30 km a day, how many years would it take to walk every road the Romans ever built?
questions.explainer: A 2025 map puts the Roman road network at about 300,000 km. At 30 km a day that is 10,000 days, about 27 years of walking.
questions.source_title: New map transforms what we know about Roman roads (Scientific American)

questions.question: How many years would it take to spend the Louisiana Purchase price of $15 million at $1,000 a day?
questions.explainer: In 1803 the US paid $15 million for the Louisiana territory. At $1,000 a day that is 15,000 days, about 41 years.

questions.question: How many golf balls would weigh the same as a family car?
questions.explainer: A golf ball weighs 45.9 g and a family car about 1,500 kg, so about 33,000 golf balls.

questions.question: How many bathtubs of milk do the world's cows produce every second?
questions.explainer: The world produces about 930 million tonnes of milk a year, roughly 930 billion litres. That is 29,000 litres a second, about 98 bathtubs.

questions.question: How many Eiffel Towers' worth of metal is there in the Golden Gate Bridge?
questions.explainer: The Golden Gate Bridge contains about 83,000 US tons of steel, 75,000 tonnes. The Eiffel Tower's iron weighs 7,300 tonnes, so about 10 Eiffel Towers.

questions.question: How many kilometres of toilet paper does the average American use in a lifetime?
questions.explainer: Americans use about 140 rolls a year, each around 30 m long. Over 80 years that is 336,000 m, about 340 km: London to Manchester.

questions.question: If the whole world's population moved to Texas, how many people would there be per square kilometre?
questions.explainer: Texas is about 695,700 km². 8.1 billion people spread over it is about 12,000 per km², a little denser than Paris today.

questions.question: Watching non-stop for a week, how many times could you get through the extended Lord of the Rings trilogy?
questions.explainer: The three extended films run about 11.4 hours together. A week is 168 hours, so about 15 times through.
questions.source_title: The Lord of the Rings (film series) (Wikipedia)

questions.question: How many customers does McDonald's serve every second, worldwide?
questions.explainer: McDonald's says it serves about 69 million customers a day. Divided by 86,400 seconds, that is about 800 people a second.

questions.question: How many words does a person speak in a lifetime?
questions.explainer: A 2007 study found people speak about 16,000 words a day. Over 75 talking years that is about 440 million words.
questions.source_title: Are Women Really More Talkative Than Men? (Science, 2007)

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools would all the gold ever mined in history fill?
questions.explainer: About 216,000 tonnes of gold have ever been mined. Gold is dense, 19,300 kg per m³, so that is only 11,200 m³: about four and a half Olympic pools.
questions.source_title: How much gold has been mined? (World Gold Council)

questions.question: How many people could stand in Central Park at four to a square metre?
questions.explainer: Central Park is 3.41 km², or 3.41 million m². At four per square metre that is about 14 million people, more than live in New York City.

questions.question: How many trips around the equator is a car's typical 300,000 km lifetime?
questions.explainer: A well-kept car covers about 300,000 km before it is scrapped. The equator is 40,075 km, so about seven and a half laps of the planet.

questions.question: How many Manhattans would fit inside Texas?
questions.explainer: Texas is about 695,700 km² and Manhattan is 59.1 km², so Texas could hold roughly 12,000 Manhattans.

questions.question: Driving non-stop at 100 km/h, how many months would it take to reach the Moon?
questions.explainer: The Moon is about 384,400 km away. At 100 km/h that is 3,844 hours, or 160 days: a bit over five months of driving.

questions.question: How many 50-seat coaches would it take to seat everyone in Greater Tokyo at once?
questions.explainer: Greater Tokyo has about 37 million people. At 50 a coach that is 740,000 coaches, a traffic jam about 9,000 km long.

questions.question: How many 5 g gold wedding rings could be made from Tutankhamun's solid gold coffin?
questions.explainer: Tutankhamun's innermost coffin is about 110 kg of gold, which is 110,000 g. At 5 g a ring that is about 22,000 wedding rings.

questions.question: How many WhatsApp messages are sent every second?
questions.explainer: WhatsApp carries about 100 billion messages a day. Divided by 86,400 seconds, that is about 1.2 million messages a second.

questions.question: If a cheetah could hold its top speed the whole way, how many minutes would it take to run a marathon?
questions.explainer: A cheetah sprints at about 110 km/h. A marathon is 42.195 km, so 42.195 ÷ 110 hours is about 23 minutes (if only it could keep it up).

questions.question: Driving non-stop at 100 km/h, how many days would it take to drive once around the equator?
questions.explainer: 40,075 km at 100 km/h is about 401 hours, which is about 17 days of driving.

questions.question: If all the hair your head grows in a lifetime were laid end to end, how many kilometres would it stretch?
questions.explainer: A head has about 100,000 hairs, each growing about 15 cm a year. Over 80 years that is 100,000 × 0.15 m × 80 = 1.2 million metres, about 1,200 km.

questions.question: How many 75-year lifetimes ago did the last woolly mammoths die out?
questions.explainer: The last mammoths, on Wrangel Island, died out about 4,000 years ago, while the pyramids already stood. That is only about 53 lifetimes back.

questions.question: How many years of non-stop listening do one billion Spotify streams of a 3.5-minute song add up to?
questions.explainer: A billion plays of 3.5 minutes is 3.5 billion minutes, 58 million hours, about 6,700 years of listening.

questions.question: How many 80,000-seat stadiums would it take to seat the entire population of China at once?
questions.explainer: China has about 1.41 billion people. Divided by 80,000 seats, that is about 18,000 stadiums.

questions.question: At ten minutes a day, how many full days of an 80-year life are spent on the toilet?
questions.explainer: Ten minutes a day for 80 years is 292,000 minutes, 4,870 hours: about 200 days sitting down.

questions.question: How many potatoes go into McDonald's fries worldwide in a year?
questions.explainer: McDonald's buys about 3.4 billion pounds of potatoes a year, about 1.54 billion kg. At 170 g a potato, that is roughly 9 billion potatoes.

questions.question: How many litres of Coca-Cola products are drunk worldwide every second?
questions.explainer: Coca-Cola serves about 2.2 billion drinks a day. At a 237 ml serving that is 521 million litres a day, about 6,000 litres every second.

questions.question: How many kilograms of toothpaste does a person squeeze out in an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: A pea-sized squeeze is about 1 g. Twice a day for 80 years is 58,400 g, about 58 kg of toothpaste: roughly your own body weight.

questions.question: How many times do you blink in a single day?
questions.explainer: People blink about 15 times a minute while awake. Over 16 waking hours that is 15 × 60 × 16, about 14,000 blinks.

questions.question: How many copies of the Mona Lisa, laid side by side, would it take to carpet a football pitch?
questions.explainer: The Mona Lisa is 77 cm by 53 cm, 0.41 m². A pitch is about 7,140 m², so about 17,000 Mona Lisas.

questions.question: How many times does the International Space Station go around the Earth in one day?
questions.explainer: One orbit takes about 92.9 minutes, so in 1,440 minutes the station laps the planet about 15.5 times. Astronauts see 16 sunrises a day.

questions.question: How many times has 'Baby Shark' been watched on YouTube for every person on Earth?
questions.explainer: The Baby Shark Dance video passed 15 billion views. Divided by 8.1 billion people, that is nearly two views each.

questions.question: How many Google searches happen every second?
questions.explainer: Google handles about 14 billion searches a day, which is about 160,000 every second.
questions.source_title: Google now sees more than 5 trillion searches per year (Search Engine Land)

questions.question: How many Pokémon trading cards have been printed for every person on Earth?
questions.explainer: The Pokémon Company had shipped 64.8 billion cards by March 2024. With 8.1 billion people, that is eight cards each.

questions.question: At 7,000 steps a day, how many steps does a person take in an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: 7,000 steps a day times 365 days times 80 years is about 200 million steps.

questions.question: For every person alive today, how many people have ever been born?
questions.explainer: Demographers estimate about 117 billion people have ever been born, against 8.1 billion alive: about 14 ancestors for each of us.
questions.source_title: How many people have ever lived on Earth? (PRB)

questions.question: Counting one star a second without a break, how many years would it take to count every star in the Milky Way?
questions.explainer: The Milky Way has roughly 100 billion stars. There are 31.6 million seconds in a year, so the count would take about 3,200 years.

questions.question: How many birthday candles does a person blow out in an 80-year life, one candle per year of age?
questions.explainer: One candle on the first birthday, two on the second, and so on up to 80: 1 + 2 + ... + 80 = 80 × 81 ÷ 2, which is 3,240 candles.

questions.question: How many football pitches would it take for everyone in India to stand four to a square metre?
questions.explainer: India's 1.43 billion people at four per square metre need 357 million m². A pitch is 7,140 m², so about 50,000 pitches.

questions.question: How many bicycles would it take to weigh the same as an empty Boeing 747?
questions.explainer: An empty 747 weighs about 180 tonnes, 180,000 kg. A bicycle weighs about 12 kg, so about 15,000 bikes.

questions.question: How many babies are born around the world every minute?
questions.explainer: About 360,000 babies are born each day. Divided by 1,440 minutes that is about 250 a minute, four every second.
questions.source_title: Births and deaths (Our World in Data)

questions.question: How many M&M's would weigh the same as a blue whale?
questions.explainer: A blue whale can weigh 150 tonnes (150,000 kg) and an M&M weighs about 0.9 g, so about 170 million M&M's.

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools of beer were drunk at Oktoberfest 2024?
questions.explainer: Munich reported 7 million litres of beer served at Oktoberfest 2024. An Olympic pool holds 2.5 million litres, so about 2.8 pools.
questions.source_title: Oktoberfest facts and figures (City of Munich)

questions.question: How many Big Macs is a year of the median US household income?
questions.explainer: The median US household earned $80,610 in 2023. At $5.69 a Big Mac that is about 14,000 burgers, 39 a day.
questions.source_title: Income in the United States: 2023 (U.S. Census Bureau)

questions.question: How many marathons laid end to end would it take to go once around the equator?
questions.explainer: The equator is 40,075 km and a marathon is 42.195 km, so about 950 marathons.

questions.question: How many full Monopoly banks would it take to buy a median-priced American home with play money?
questions.explainer: A Monopoly set comes with $20,580 of play money and the median US home sold for about $420,000 in 2024, so about 20 full banks.

questions.question: If every tennis ball used at one Wimbledon were stacked in a single column, how many kilometres tall would it be?
questions.explainer: Wimbledon uses about 55,000 balls a tournament. At 6.7 cm each the column would be about 3.7 km tall, higher than most mountains in Britain.

questions.question: Shaking hands for three seconds each, eight hours a day, how many years would it take to shake hands with everyone on Earth?
questions.explainer: 8.1 billion handshakes of 3 seconds is 24.3 billion seconds. At 28,800 seconds of shaking a day that is 844,000 days, about 2,300 years.

questions.question: How many chickens are alive right now for every person on Earth?
questions.explainer: There are about 27 billion chickens alive at any moment and 8.1 billion people, so more than three chickens each.
questions.source_title: How many chickens are in the world? (The Humane League)

questions.question: How much would it cost to buy every possible Powerball ticket combination at $2 each?
questions.explainer: There are 292,201,338 possible Powerball combinations. At $2 a ticket that is about $584 million, so a jackpot below that loses money even if you buy them all.

questions.question: If all your blood vessels were laid end to end, how many times would they wrap around the equator?
questions.explainer: The usual estimate is about 100,000 km of blood vessels in an adult, most of it tiny capillaries. The equator is 40,075 km, so about two and a half times around.

questions.question: For every Harry Potter book ever sold, how many people are there on Earth?
questions.explainer: More than 600 million Harry Potter books have been sold. With 8.1 billion people, that is one book for every 14 of us.

questions.question: How many standard 2x4 LEGO bricks would it take to build a solid, full-size London double-decker bus?
questions.explainer: A New Routemaster is about 11.2 m long, 2.5 m wide and 4.4 m tall, about 124 m³, or 124 million cm³. A 2x4 brick is about 4.8 cm³, so about 26 million bricks.

questions.question: How many kilometres does an Arctic tern fly in its lifetime?
questions.explainer: An Arctic tern migrates pole to pole, about 70,000 km a year, and can live 30 years: about 2.1 million km, three return trips to the Moon.

questions.question: How many Grand Canyons could you fill with all the water in North America's Great Lakes?
questions.explainer: The Great Lakes hold about 22,700 km³ of water and the Grand Canyon has a volume of roughly 4,170 km³, so the lakes would fill it about five and a half times.

questions.question: How many rolls of toilet paper, unrolled end to end, would it take to reach the Moon?
questions.explainer: The Moon is 384,400 km away, 384.4 million metres. At about 30 m a roll, that is about 13 million rolls.

questions.question: If every pet dog in the United States ate 300 g of food a day, how many tonnes of dog food would that be each day?
questions.explainer: The AVMA counts about 89.7 million pet dogs in the US. At 0.3 kg each that is 26.9 million kg a day, about 27,000 tonnes.

questions.question: How many football pitches, laid side by side, would it take to carpet the whole Sahara Desert?
questions.explainer: The Sahara covers about 9.2 million km², and a full-size pitch is 105 m by 68 m, or 7,140 m². That is 9.2 trillion m² divided by 7,140: about 1.3 billion pitches.

questions.question: How many kilometres tall would a stack of one trillion one-dollar bills be?
questions.explainer: A dollar bill is about 0.11 mm thick. A trillion of them is 110 million metres, about 110,000 km: more than a quarter of the way to the Moon.

questions.question: How many Eiffel Towers stacked end to end would reach from the sea surface to the bottom of the Mariana Trench?
questions.explainer: The Challenger Deep is about 10,935 m down and the Eiffel Tower is 330 m tall, so it would take about 33 towers.

questions.question: How many human hairs laid side by side would it take to span one metre?
questions.explainer: A human hair is about 70 micrometres (0.07 mm) wide, so 1,000 mm divided by 0.07 mm is roughly 14,000 hairs.

questions.question: At 7,000 steps a day, how many kilometres does a person walk in an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: 7,000 steps of about 0.75 m is 5.25 km a day. Over 80 years that is about 150,000 km, nearly four times around the Earth.

questions.question: How many football pitches would fit inside Vatican City?
questions.explainer: Vatican City is only 0.49 km², or 490,000 m². A full-size pitch is about 7,140 m², so the whole country is about 69 pitches.

questions.question: How many pedal strokes does a Tour de France winner make over the whole race?
questions.explainer: The 2024 winner rode for about 84 hours. At a typical 90 revolutions a minute, that is 84 × 60 × 90, about 450,000 pedal strokes.

questions.question: How many honeybees live in the world's managed beehives for every person on Earth?
questions.explainer: The FAO counts about 102 million managed hives, each home to roughly 30,000 bees: 3 trillion bees, about 380 per person.

questions.question: How many laps of a 400 m running track is the Tour de France?
questions.explainer: The 2024 Tour was 3,498 km, which is 3,498,000 m. Divided by a 400 m track that is about 8,700 laps.

questions.question: How many hours of Simpsons would you have watched if you saw every episode the week it aired, from 1989 to 2025?
questions.explainer: 790 episodes of 22 minutes is 17,380 minutes, which is about 290 hours: twelve full days of Springfield spread over 36 years.

questions.question: How many footballs would it take to fill Wembley's pitch to a depth of one metre?
questions.explainer: The pitch is 105 m by 68 m, so a metre deep is 7,140 m³. A 22 cm football is 5.6 litres, and balls pack to about 64%, so about 820,000 footballs.

questions.question: How many full days a year does the average American driver spend behind the wheel?
questions.explainer: Americans drive about 13,500 miles a year, 21,700 km. At an average 50 km/h that is 434 hours, about 18 full days a year.

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools would all the coffee the world drinks in one day fill?
questions.explainer: The world drinks about 2.25 billion cups a day. At 250 ml a cup that is 560 million litres, and a pool holds 2.5 million litres: about 230 pools.
questions.source_title: How much coffee the world drinks (Tasting Table)

questions.question: To finish the Great Pyramid in 20 years, how many stone blocks did its builders have to set every day?
questions.explainer: The pyramid has about 2.3 million blocks. Over 20 years, 7,305 days, that is about 315 blocks a day: one every few minutes, day and night.

questions.question: Walking at 5 km/h non-stop, how many days would it take to walk all the way around the Moon's equator?
questions.explainer: The Moon's equator is about 10,921 km around. At 5 km/h that is 2,184 hours, or about 91 days.

questions.question: Working full time on the US federal minimum wage, how many years would it take to earn a million dollars?
questions.explainer: $7.25 an hour for 2,080 hours a year is $15,080 a year. A million dollars takes about 66 years, before tax.

questions.question: How many dairy cows would it take to weigh the same as the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explainer: The statue weighs about 204 tonnes and a dairy cow about 700 kg, so roughly 290 cows.

questions.question: If everything since the Great Pyramid was built were squeezed into one 24-hour day, how many minutes would the World Wide Web have existed?
questions.explainer: The pyramid is about 4,570 years old and the Web went public in 1991, about 35 years ago. 35 ÷ 4,570 of a 1,440-minute day is about 11 minutes.

questions.question: How many grains of rice does the average person in Asia eat in a year?
questions.explainer: People in rice-eating countries get through about 100 kg a year. A grain weighs about 25 mg, so 100,000 g ÷ 0.025 g is about 4 million grains.

questions.question: Spending $1,000 every second, how many years would it take to spend Jeff Bezos's 2025 fortune?
questions.explainer: Forbes put Bezos at about $215 billion in 2025. At $1,000 a second that is 215 million seconds, about 6.8 years.

questions.question: How many Big Macs would a Tour de France rider need to replace all the energy burned over the three-week race?
questions.explainer: Riders burn about 6,000 kcal a day for 21 stages, about 126,000 kcal. At 590 kcal a Big Mac, that is about 210 burgers.

questions.question: How many times would you have to fold a sheet of paper in half for the stack to reach the Moon?
questions.explainer: Each fold doubles the thickness. Starting from 0.1 mm, after 42 folds the stack is 0.0001 m × 2⁴² = 440,000 km, past the Moon's 384,400 km.

questions.question: Running non-stop at the marathon world-record pace, how many days would it take to run around the world?
questions.explainer: The record is 2:00:35, which is 21 km/h. 40,075 km at that speed is 1,909 hours, about 80 days, with no sleep.

questions.question: How many pennies stacked on top of each other would reach the height of Mount Everest?
questions.explainer: A US penny is 1.52 mm thick and Everest is 8,849 m tall, so about 5.8 million pennies, worth about $58,000.

questions.question: How many hours a year does the average American spend commuting to and from work?
questions.explainer: The average one-way commute is 26.8 minutes. Two trips a day for 250 working days is 13,400 minutes, about 220 hours: nine days a year.

questions.question: How many ants are there on Earth for every single person?
questions.explainer: A 2022 study estimated 20 quadrillion ants. Divided by 8.1 billion people, that is about 2.5 million ants each.
questions.source_title: The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth (PNAS, 2022)

questions.question: How many times does the average American check their phone in a year?
questions.explainer: A 2024 survey found Americans check their phones about 205 times a day. Over a year that is about 75,000 glances.

questions.question: How many Titanics would fit inside Icon of the Seas, the world's largest cruise ship, by gross tonnage?
questions.explainer: Icon of the Seas measures 250,800 gross tons; the Titanic measured 46,328. That is about 5.4 Titanics.
questions.source_title: Icon of the Seas vs Titanic (Cruise Hive)

questions.question: How many cups of coffee does the average Finn drink in a year?
questions.explainer: Finns drink about 10 kg of roasted coffee each per year, the most in the world. At 8 g a cup that is about 1,250 cups: three and a half a day.

questions.question: How many passengers pass through Atlanta's airport, the world's busiest, every minute?
questions.explainer: Hartsfield-Jackson handled 108.1 million passengers in 2024. A year has 525,960 minutes, so about 210 passengers a minute, day and night.

questions.question: Over a 60-year driving life, how many whole years does the average American spend driving?
questions.explainer: About 434 hours a year behind the wheel, times 60 years, is 26,000 hours: about 3 years of your life in the driver's seat.

questions.question: Reading at 250 words a minute, how many hours would it take to read everything Shakespeare wrote?
questions.explainer: Shakespeare's complete works run to 884,647 words. At 250 a minute that is 3,539 minutes, about 59 hours.

questions.question: How many basketballs would it take to fill the Grand Canyon?
questions.explainer: The canyon's volume is about 4,170 km³, or 4.17 × 10¹² m³. A 24 cm basketball is 7.2 litres, and balls pack to about 64%, so roughly 370 trillion basketballs.

questions.question: How many keystrokes does an office worker type in a year?
questions.explainer: A typical desk job runs to about 8,000 keystrokes a day. Over 250 working days that is about 2 million key presses.

questions.question: If all the hot dogs Americans eat on the Fourth of July were laid end to end, how many kilometres would they stretch?
questions.explainer: Americans eat about 150 million hot dogs on the Fourth. At 15 cm each that is 22.5 million metres, about 23,000 km: more than halfway round the Earth.
questions.source_title: Hot dog consumption (National Hot Dog and Sausage Council)

questions.question: How many times does a hummingbird beat its wings in an hour?
questions.explainer: A hummingbird beats its wings about 50 times a second, and there are 3,600 seconds in an hour: about 180,000 beats.

questions.question: How many Olympic swimming pools could the Amazon River fill every second?
questions.explainer: The Amazon pours about 209,000 m³ into the Atlantic every second, and an Olympic pool holds 2,500 m³: roughly 84 pools a second.

questions.question: How many fully loaded jumbo jets would weigh the same as the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.explainer: The Great Pyramid weighs about 5.9 million tonnes and a fully loaded Boeing 747 about 400 tonnes, so about 15,000 jumbo jets.

questions.question: How many Central Parks would fit inside Greenland?
questions.explainer: Greenland is about 2,166,000 km² and Central Park is 3.41 km², so Greenland could hold roughly 640,000 Central Parks.

questions.question: How many bathtubs would it take to hold all the water in Lake Baikal?
questions.explainer: Baikal holds about 23,600 km³, which is 23.6 trillion m³. A full bathtub is about 300 litres (0.3 m³), so you would need roughly 79 trillion of them.

questions.question: How many bathtubs of rain fall on Greater London in a typical year?
questions.explainer: Greater London is 1,572 km² and gets about 600 mm of rain a year, so 1.572 billion m² × 0.6 m is 943 million m³ of water. At 300 litres a tub, that is about 3.1 billion bathtubs.

questions.question: How many apples go into one litre of apple juice?
questions.explainer: It takes about 1.5 kg of apples to press a litre of juice. A medium apple is about 180 g, so roughly 8 apples per litre.

questions.question: How many flights take off somewhere in the world every minute?
questions.explainer: About 100,000 commercial flights take off every day. Divided by 1,440 minutes that is about 69 a minute, more than one a second.
questions.source_title: How many aeroplanes head for the skies each day (Air Dolomiti)

questions.question: How many London buses parked end to end would it take to stretch across the English Channel at its narrowest?
questions.explainer: The Strait of Dover is 33.3 km wide and a New Routemaster is 11.2 m long, so about 3,000 buses.

questions.question: How many litres of saliva does a person produce in a lifetime?
questions.explainer: A healthy adult makes about a litre of saliva a day, so over 80 years that is roughly 29,000 litres: a dozen Olympic pools' worth of bathtubs.

questions.question: If every person on Earth chipped in one dollar, how many brand-new Boeing 747s could you buy?
questions.explainer: 8.1 billion dollars at a list price of about $400 million a 747-8 buys about 20 jumbo jets.

questions.question: How many bathtubs of water does one person use showering over an 80-year life?
questions.explainer: A shower uses about 65 litres. One a day for 80 years is 1.9 million litres, which is about 6,300 bathtubs of 300 litres.

questions.question: Counting one bill a second non-stop, how many days would it take to count a million dollars in $1 bills?
questions.explainer: There are 86,400 seconds in a day, so a million seconds is about 11.6 days of non-stop counting.

questions.question: How many bathtubs of jet fuel does a Boeing 747 burn on a 10-hour flight?
questions.explainer: A 747 burns about 11 tonnes an hour, so 110 tonnes in 10 hours. Jet fuel weighs 0.8 kg a litre, so that is 137,000 litres: about 460 bathtubs.
questions.source_title: How much fuel does a jumbo jet burn? (Flight Deck Friend)

questions.question: How many tennis balls would fit inside a London double-decker bus?
questions.explainer: A double-decker has roughly 100 m³ of space inside. A tennis ball is 6.7 cm across (0.000157 m³) and balls pack to about 64%, so about 410,000 balls.

questions.question: How many kilometres does a Premier League outfield player run over a full 38-game season?
questions.explainer: Outfield players cover about 11 km a match. Over 38 matches that is about 420 km, London to Newcastle on foot.

questions.question: How much does a $4 coffee every single day add up to over 60 years?
questions.explainer: $4 a day is $1,461 a year. Over 60 years that is about $88,000, a decent car for every decade.

questions.question: How many smartphones are sold worldwide every second?
questions.explainer: About 1.24 billion smartphones shipped in 2024. Divided by 31.6 million seconds, that is about 39 phones a second.

questions.question: At the world's birth rate, how many new people arrive every time your heart beats, over a day?
questions.explainer: About 360,000 babies are born a day while a resting heart beats about 100,800 times, so roughly 3.6 babies per heartbeat.
questions.source_title: Births and deaths (Our World in Data)

questions.question: How many years would it take to watch all the video uploaded to YouTube in a single day?
questions.explainer: 500 hours a minute times 1,440 minutes is 720,000 hours of video a day. Watching 24/7, that is about 82 years, a whole lifetime for one day's uploads.
questions.source_title: Hours of video uploaded to YouTube every minute (Statista)

questions.question: Flying at a jumbo jet's 900 km/h, how many years would it take to reach Proxima Centauri, the nearest star?
questions.explainer: Proxima Centauri is about 40 trillion km away. At 900 km/h that is 4.4 × 10¹⁰ hours, which is about 5.1 million years.

questions.question: How many sheep are there in New Zealand for every person?
questions.explainer: New Zealand counted 23.6 million sheep in 2024 and has about 5.2 million people: about 4.5 sheep each, down from 22 in 1982.
questions.source_title: New Zealand ratio of sheep per person drops to 4.5:1 (Agriland)

questions.question: If all the ice in Antarctica were cut into Olympic swimming pool-sized blocks, how many blocks would there be?
questions.explainer: The Antarctic ice sheet holds about 26.5 million km³ of ice, which is 2.65 × 10¹⁶ m³. Divided by a 2,500 m³ pool that is about 11 trillion blocks.

questions.question: How many Oreos are baked every second, worldwide?
questions.explainer: Mondelez bakes about 40 billion Oreos a year in 18 countries. That works out to about 1,300 cookies every second.

questions.question: How many ants would it take to weigh the same as one adult person?
questions.explainer: A typical ant weighs about 3 mg and an adult about 70 kg (70,000 g), so it would take roughly 23 million ants.

questions.question: How many bananas would you have to eat to get a whole year's worth of calories?
questions.explainer: An adult needs about 2,000 kcal a day, 730,000 a year. A banana has about 105 kcal, so about 7,000 bananas, 19 a day.

questions.question: How many iPhones stacked flat on top of each other would reach the top of the Empire State Building?
questions.explainer: The Empire State Building is 443 m to its tip and an iPhone 15 is 7.8 mm thick: about 57,000 phones.

questions.question: How many 25-year generations separate us from the fall of the Western Roman Empire in AD 476?
questions.explainer: From 476 to 2026 is 1,550 years. At 25 years a generation that is about 62 generations: a line of 62 parents and children.
questions.source_title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire (Wikipedia)

questions.question: How many litres of water does a tap dripping once a second waste in a year?
questions.explainer: A drip is about 0.05 ml. One a second for a year's 31.6 million seconds is about 1,600 litres, five bathtubs down the drain.

questions.question: On average, how many seconds pass between one aircraft movement and the next at London Heathrow?
questions.explainer: Heathrow handles about 475,000 take-offs and landings a year, about 1,300 a day. 86,400 seconds divided by 1,300 is one every 66 seconds or so.

questions.question: How many teaspoons of water does it take to fill a bathtub?
questions.explainer: A full bath is about 300 litres and a teaspoon is 5 ml, so 300,000 ml divided by 5 ml is 60,000 teaspoons.

questions.question: How many eggs do the world's hens lay every second?
questions.explainer: The world produces about 1.6 trillion eggs a year. Divided by 31.6 million seconds, that is about 51,000 eggs a second.

questions.question: How many bananas laid end to end would it take to reach from Paris to Berlin?
questions.explainer: Paris to Berlin is about 878 km in a straight line, 878,000 m. A banana is about 18 cm long, so about 4.9 million bananas.
